findings.reason: a node reading §19 would either rebuild an existing guard or discover mid-flight that the fix it needs is in a module it cannot write, and the section's own claim about the defect is false for half the instances it cites.
findings.text: §19's premise that a cli pointer in `starting` with no worker record past the bound "read as running indefinitely" is already contradicted at HEAD: `_stranded_launch` (`reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:746`, bound `STRANDED_LAUNCH_BOUND_SECONDS = 900` at :68) is reached above the in-harness arm at `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:2065` and classifies exactly that shape as `launch-failed`, and `tests/test_a_run_stuck_before_launch_is_reported.py` already builds it with `"launch": "cli"`, `phase: "starting"`, no worker record and no stream. The only shape left falling through to the in-harness sentence at :2147 is one `_attempt_started_seconds` cannot date (that function returns None when neither `attempt_started_at` nor an attempt record exists) — which the section never names, and whose repair lives in `recovery_liveness.py`, outside its declared write paths

findings.reason: a control that is green at base proves nothing, and an unmeasured deliverable is one a review cannot close the section on.
findings.text: §19's negative control ("classifying by phase alone makes the first case read as running") does not hold at base for a pointer that records a launch clock, where base already reads `launch-failed`; and the deliverable "traces why these reflex launches wrote a pointer and spawned nothing, and names the launch path in its manifest" has no measure and no control, so a node can deliver the test and skip it

findings.reason: the dispatch fence grants the literal path, so a node would be granted a file that is not the module, and the real module it must edit would sit outside its write scope.
findings.text: §20's write paths name `reckon/crew/_backends.py`, which does not exist; the LaunchPlan and fence helpers it means live in `reckon/_backends.py` (3,260 lines), imported as `from reckon import _backends` at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:47`

findings.reason: the claim is true and the section's done declaration stands on :2358 and on `tests/test_dispatch_reads_the_fleet_record_through_its_owner.py`, so only the pointer a later reader follows is wrong.
findings.text: the section-18 reconciliation comment cites `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2243-2248` as where "the record is resolved through fleet_supervisor.state_directory"; those lines are the supervisor survival loop (`process_alive`, `time.monotonic() >= deadline`), and the resolution is at :2353-2358 (`state_directory() / RECORD_NAME`),

findings.reason: §20's done-when already requires the composed environment to carry the directory, so a resolver added only at preflight fails the section's own test rather than surviving.
findings.text: §20 requires the directory found on the declared path to be "added to the worker's PATH" but names only `preflight_launch_command` (`dispatch_launch.py:1061`); the one function through which both the refusal and the composed environment run is `launch_search_path` (`dispatch_launch.py:608`, called at :695 to write the persisted `PATH`, and at :1127, :1241, :1477)
